All 9 rows share the stem "Quanto sei d accordo che le seguenti affermazioni descrivano la tua esperienza di apprendimento in questo semestre", shipped once in `instructions`; `item_text` holds the item-specific statement. INSTRUMENT IDENTIFICATION: the paper (sec. 3.2.6) names the Student Engagement Scale of Mameli & Passini (2017); the deposit's 43 ENG_* columns split 9/12/12/10 exactly as that paper's affective (9) / behavioural (12) / cognitive (12) / agentic (10, AES) subscales, and ENG_COMP is behavioural ("comportamentale"), not "comprehensive". All 9 Italian items back-translate onto the SESQ affective block of Hart et al. (2011) Table 3 one-for-one: ENG_EMO_01=a7, 02=a5, 03=a3, 04=a17, 05=a15, 06=a11, 07=a13, 08=a1, 09=a9R. VERIFICATION (verify_merlo2025_eng_emotional.R, VERDICT: PASS): although data_labels is exempt, the deposit-column-to-live-item link was checked anyway -- all 9 live per-item means equal the corresponding deposit column means to 0.00e+00, and the 9 means are pairwise distinct (closest pair ENG_EMO_03 4.462911 vs ENG_EMO_07 4.473239, gap 0.01033), so any permutation of the codes would break the test for every permuted item. REVERSE SCORING (this is the substantive finding): ENG_EMO_09 "Penso che studiare sia noioso" (I think studying is boring) is stored ALREADY REVERSED in the deposit. It correlates +0.205 to +0.386 with all eight positively worded items -- impossible for a raw negatively worded item -- and Cronbach alpha on the columns as stored is 0.8902 against 0.8196 with item 09 flipped, the former matching the published affective alpha of .87. The same pattern holds for the three reverse-worded behavioural items in the same deposit file (ENG_COMP_02/04/09 all correlate positively with the positive items), so the deposit is pre-recoded throughout rather than this being a one-item quirk. CONSEQUENCE FOR option_text: ENG_EMO_09 ships the anchors REVERSED relative to the other eight (resp 1 = Totally agree, resp 7 = Completely disagree), because option_text has to describe what the STORED value means; the burkert_2019_whoqol_bref precedent in the skill (anchors reversed to match the data) is the model. OPTION AXIS otherwise: the deposit publishes no value labels and the administered Italian anchors are published nowhere. The coding is stated outright by both papers -- Merlo et al. sec. 3.2.6, "a scale ranging from completely disagree (1) to totally agree (7) in the affective, behavioural and agentic engagement subscales", and Mameli & Passini (2017), "a 7-point Likert scale (from 1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree)". Route 8 agrees: ENG_EMO_05 "In genere non vedo l ora di andare a scuola" is the least endorsed item at 2.99 and ENG_EMO_08 "Sono molto interessato a imparare" the most at 4.91, which for 1065 adolescents (mean age 15.95) is only readable under 1 = disagree. NOT ESTABLISHED: only the two ENDS of the 7-point scale are pinned; the five interior points ship with option_text blank because no anchor exists for them, and they were NOT padded with their own numbers. RIGHTS: no block, and this one needed care because the instrument is a named published scale under a permissive deposit. The originator of the ADMINISTERED Italian wording is Mameli & Passini (2017). Their TPM article reserves nothing over the instrument: the only relevant sentences are "Copies of the Italian questionnaire are available from the authors on request" and note 3, "The precise formulation of the Italian items composing the questionnaire is available from the authors upon request" -- both describe how to obtain a copy, not a condition on reuse, and neither names a fee, a permission requirement, a non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term (compare the SAQ-SF row in the register, where an optional permission-letter mechanism was ruled not to be a condition). The article PDF carries "(c) 2017 Cises / Green Open Access under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International License", which is the journal's licence on the ARTICLE -- and the article does not contain the Italian items at all (note 3 says they are available on request), so it cannot be the term governing wording it does not print. The source column names are bare Qualtrics block codes (Q1_1..Q7_7) carrying no labels of any kind, so the exemption buys nothing: the text still has to be tied to the codes by inference, hence mapping_basis=paper_order rather than data_labels. TEXT: Double (2025) Supplementary Materials (OSF 4jyxb, 'Supplementary Materials.docx'), which prints the 64-item pool as a numbered list; transcribed verbatim via python-docx, including the study's own typos and punctuation ('I am a aware of my strengths and weaknesses', the trailing period on 'I prioritize performance monitoring, even when I'm busy.', and the curly apostrophes in 'I'm doing' / 'don't'). MAPPING: the live table has 67 items against the paper's stated 64-item pool. The study's own analysis script (ex1-self-reports-metacognition-analysis.R) takes the columns Q1_1..Q7_7 and removes exactly three -- Q6_5 and Q7_6 ('Remove attention check') and Q3_7 ('Remove repeated item') -- leaving 64. Aligning the supplement's items 1..64 to the 64 retained columns in file order is the only alignment consistent with that, and it is verified against the supplement's own two-factor promax loading table: re-running factanal(items, 2, rotation='promax') on the live IRW data reproduces all 64 published loading pairs exactly (largest deviation 0.0000000; e.g. Q1_1 -0.1377552/0.86704274, Q7_5 -0.7747929/0.25953941). See verify_metacogmonitoring_double2025.R. BLANK ITEM_TEXT (3 of 67): Q6_5 and Q7_6 are the two instructed-response attention checks (298/300 respondents answered 5 and 297/300 answered 2; the paper gives only an example wording, 'e.g., "Please select Disagree to show you are paying attention"', so no literal wording is recoverable for either). Q3_7 is the repeated item; the supplement's list carries each wording once, so which one it repeats is not published. Its highest correlation is with Q3_4 (r=0.78, 75% exact agreement; next-highest Q2_6 r=0.61, 58%), which is suggestive but not published, so nothing is shipped for it. OPTIONS: the paper states only the endpoints -- 'Each item was rated on a Likert-like scale from 1 - "Strongly Disagree" to 6 - "Strongly Agree"'. Points 2-5 carry no published label and are left blank rather than padded. (The quoted attention-check example plus the script's expected value of 2 for Q7_6 imply point 2 is labelled 'Disagree', but the paper flags that wording as an example, so it is recorded here rather than shipped.) INSTRUCTIONS: none published; left blank. STEP 3b: matches -- 67 items on a 1-6 agreement scale, and the four items the paper quotes by wording land on the four CFA marker items of the matching factor (monitoring: Q1_3 'I deliberately assess my performance on all tasks', Q1_7 'I evaluate how confident I am after each decision'; self-awareness: Q2_6 'I am a aware of my strengths and weaknesses', Q2_7 'I know when I am performing well'). This is a new item pool written for this study, not a named published instrument. RIGHTS: no block and nothing to quote. The items are the authors' own, first published in the Supplementary Materials of a CC BY 4.0 article (Behav Res Methods 57:97, PMC11836092) with an open OSF deposit; no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause appears in the article, the supplement or the OSF project, and instrument_rights_register.csv has no matching row (checked by instrument name and by item wording).
